v.why: Removing edge 5 hurts more when the direct input-output edge is absent, since fewer paths to the output remain.
With edge 4 absent, removing edge 5 eliminates most or all routes into node 3, causing a severe drop.
Adding a residual skip where there was no edge helps far more than replacing an existing conv on that edge.
Restoring a missing node-2-to-output branch with a conv gives a much larger gain than swapping out another op.
When edge 5 is none, node 2 is disconnected from the output, so changing edge 1 has almost no effect.
Removing edge 0 when edge 1 is also absent leaves only the direct edge, so the loss is larger.
Adding avg pool on an empty edge adds a path, whereas replacing a conv with pooling loses capacity.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 carries no input signal, so a conv on edge 4 contributes little.
A skip reconnecting node 2 to the output beats having no edge, but replacing a conv with skip reduces depth and capacity.
Placing a conv on a previously empty input-output edge adds a new path, unlike replacing an existing useful op.

raw:
Ten hypotheses below, chosen using prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201's structure. None of the 100 experiments has results, so they are untested.

**Removing edge 5 (node 2 → node 3)**
1. Setting edge 5 to `none` hurts more when edge 3 is `none`. With fewer remaining paths into the output node, losing the node-2 branch costs more.
2. Setting edge 5 to `none` hurts more when edge 4 is `none`. If edges 3 and 4 are both `none`, the cell is cut off entirely.

**Filling an empty edge versus replacing an existing op**
3. Setting edge 3 to `skip_connect` helps more when edge 3 was `none`. It then adds a residual path instead of replacing a conv.
4. Setting edge 5 to `nor_conv_3x3` helps more when edge 5 was `none`. It restores a whole branch instead of swapping one op.
5. Setting edge 4 to `avg_pool_3x3` scores better when edge 4 was `none`. It adds a path instead of displacing the stronger `nor_conv_3x3`.
6. Setting edge 5 to `skip_connect` scores better when edge 5 was `none`. It reconnects node 2 instead of replacing a conv.
7. Setting edge 3 to `nor_conv_3x3` helps more when edge 3 was `none`. It adds a new path instead of competing with an existing op.

**Edits on edges that become dead**
8. Setting edge 1 to `nor_conv_3x3` has less effect when edge 5 is `none`. Node 2 then has no way to reach the output, so edge 1's op barely matters.
9. Setting edge 4 to `nor_conv_3x3` helps less when edge 0 is `none`. Node 1 then carries no input signal, so edge 4 adds little.

**Losing an alternative path**
10. Setting edge 0 to `none` hurts more when edge 1 is also `none`. Only the direct edge-3 path from the input would then remain.
